title: Numbers 5: Two of These, Two of Those (два with neuter nouns)
titleRussian: Числа 5: два с существительными среднего рода
description: We extend yesterday's two rule to neuter nouns. Два окна, два письма, два моря. Same rule as masculine: the noun gains an -а in the genitive singular. A short, focused lesson that fills the last gender slot for two.
descriptionRussian: Продолжаем правило 'два' и распространяем его на средний род. Два окна, два письма, два моря. Та же логика, что и у мужского рода: окончание -а в родительном падеже единственного числа.
intro: Neuter nouns finish the job lesson 4 started, and they side with the masculines rather than forming a third category. That is worth noticing, because it simplifies the decision you actually have to make: the gender question for two is not three-way at all. It collapses into a single yes or no, asked once, before you speak. A short lesson that exists to close a gap, and closing it now costs less than tripping over it later.
rules: Neuter nouns after 'два' take the genitive singular ending: -о switches to -а (окно → окна), -е switches to -я (море → моря).
Two with neuter nouns uses the form 'два' (same as masculine). Feminine remains the only gender that takes the separate form 'две'.
When deciding the form of two, ask only one question: is the noun feminine? Yes → две. No (masculine or neuter) → два.
The form окна (and other neuter forms in -а / -я) can look identical to the nominative plural. The number in front of it tells you which role is operating.
Three and four (Lesson 6) follow the same rule as two, with no gender forms to remember.
examples: У меня два окна. (I have two windows.) Neuter -о → -а: окно → окна.
Это два письма. (These are two letters.) Neuter -о → -а: письмо → письма.
На карте два моря. (There are two seas on the map.) Neuter -е → -я: море → моря.
У Антона два яблока. (Anton has two apples.) Neuter -о → -а: яблоко → яблока.
У меня два брата. (I have two brothers.) Yesterday's pattern: masculine -а still works.
У Лены две сестры. (Lena has two sisters.) Yesterday's pattern: feminine takes две.

tables.title: The Form of Two by Gender

items.promptEnglish: Recap from Lesson 4: I have two brothers.
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 4. Брат is masculine, so the form is 'два'. Today we extend the same form to neuter nouns: два окна, два письма.

items.hint: Switch the neuter -о of окно to -а.
items.explanation: Окно is neuter. Neuter -о switches to -а after 'два': окно → окна.
Письмо is neuter. Same pattern as окно: -о → -а. Письмо → письма. The form 'два письма' lines up neuter with masculine: both use два and both gain an -а.

items.promptEnglish: There are two seas on the map.
items.hint: Море ends in -е (soft neuter). Switch -е to its soft partner -я.
items.explanation: Море is neuter with a soft -е ending. The soft sibling of -а is -я, so -е switches to -я: море → моря. Same idea as окно → окна, just on the soft side of the sound system.

items.prompt: Which form of two fits the word «яблоко» (apple)?
items.promptEnglish: Which form of two fits the word «яблоко» (apple)?
items.hint: Яблоко is neuter. What form does two take with neuter nouns?
items.explanation: Яблоко is neuter, and neuter takes the same form as masculine: 'два'. The full phrase: два яблока. Two is feminine ('две') only when the noun itself is feminine.
Яблоко is neuter. Neuter -о switches to -а after 'два': яблоко → яблока. The two-step check is now reflex: pick the form of two (masc/neut = два, fem = две), then change the noun's ending.

errorCorrection.sentence: У меня два книги на столе.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I have two books on the table.
errorCorrection.explanation: Книга is feminine, and feminine nouns take the form две: две книги. Два is used with masculine and neuter nouns ('два окна', 'два стола').

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There are two words in this sentence.
errorCorrection.explanation: After два (or две / три / четыре), the noun goes into the GENITIVE SINGULAR: слова (gen sg of слово, -о → -а).

errorCorrection.sentence: У Антона два место в театре.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton has two seats at the theatre.
errorCorrection.explanation: After два, the noun goes into the genitive singular: места (gen sg of место, -о → -а).

minimalPairs.explanation: After 'два' the neuter noun takes the genitive singular: окно → окна. The dictionary form окно cannot follow a number; the ending must shift.
Море is neuter with soft -е; the gen sg replaces -е with -я: море → моря. The form море on its own would only fit the nominative ('this is a sea').

reviewVocab.definition: neuter gender (nouns ending in -о or -е; after 'два' they take -а or -я)
reviewVocab.example: Слово 'окно' — средний род. После 'два' окончание -о меняется на -а: 'два окна'.

reviewVocab.definition: soft ending (the soft sibling of a vowel ending; -е is the soft -о, -я is the soft -а)
reviewVocab.example: Слово 'море' имеет мягкое окончание -е, поэтому в родительном падеже единственного числа стоит мягкое -я: 'два моря'.

reviewVocab.definition: form homonymy (when two grammatical forms look the same; here, gen sg окна and nom pl окна)
reviewVocab.example: Форма 'окна' может быть и родительным падежом единственного числа после 'два' ('два окна'), и именительным падежом множественного числа ('окна стоят в ряд'). Контекст всегда подскажет роль.
